cutoff_window.rule: Only public sources with visible publication or update dates inside this window are included. Date-only June 25 candidates are excluded as ambiguous boundary-day items unless a visible timestamp proves they are after the cutoff.

federation_boundary.local_scope: Practice-level implications for AI-assisted development, including operating rules, workflows, verification, governance, and adoption.
federation_boundary.upstream_scope: Broad ecosystem coverage for companies, products, models, developer tools, agentic frameworks, MCP servers, and broad techniques is owned by /Users/martinbechard/dev/ai-wiki/docs/wiki.
federation_boundary.handling: Findings name upstream-owned entities for routing but keep summaries focused on the local practice implication.

findings.summary: OpenAI published findings from its agent work analysis, emphasizing a shift from chat-style assistance toward delegated task execution, monitoring, and human oversight patterns.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This supports local guidance that agent workflows should define delegation boundaries, review checkpoints, and escalation paths instead of treating coding assistants as single-turn completion tools.
findings.routing_note: Route broad OpenAI company and product coverage upstream; local wiki may capture delegation and oversight operating practices.

findings.summary: OpenAI described GPT-5.6 Sol as improving on coding and terminal-oriented benchmarks and discussed more capable agent execution behavior.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Model-capability announcements should feed local practice only through harness and evaluation changes: terminal task suites, regression repair checks, permissions, and reviewer gates must be updated before expanding autonomy.
findings.routing_note: Route model and benchmark background upstream; local wiki may record benchmark-to-acceptance-gate practice implications.

findings.summary: GitHub reported improved Copilot code review efficiency for repositories with many open pull requests by reducing unnecessary context gathering.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Code review agents should prefer scoped retrieval, avoid wasteful repository-wide context expansion, and make context-gathering costs observable in review harnesses.
findings.routing_note: Route GitHub and Copilot product coverage upstream; local wiki may capture scoped retrieval and review-efficiency practice.

findings.summary: GitHub announced strict known marketplace enforcement that blocks workflow actions from unverified sources.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Agent-generated CI and automation changes need package, action, and tool provenance checks before execution, especially when agents can edit workflows or install dependencies.
findings.routing_note: Route platform details upstream; local wiki may capture the governed dependency and workflow-action approval practice.

findings.summary: GitHub described preventive npm account takedowns as an account-security control for package ecosystem risk.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Coding-agent workflows that add packages should include dependency-source checks, lockfile review, and package-risk notes rather than accepting generated install commands unexamined.
findings.routing_note: Route ecosystem and npm service details upstream; local wiki may capture package-install risk gates.

findings.summary: GitHub added reporting for total merges by adoption phase in enterprise and organization reports.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Team adoption should be measured with workflow-stage metrics such as suggested, accepted, reviewed, and merged changes, not only assistant usage counts.
findings.routing_note: Route product-reporting feature details upstream; local wiki may capture adoption telemetry patterns.

findings.summary: GitHub made MAI-Code-1 Flash generally available in Copilot for Business and Enterprise.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Multi-model coding environments need model-routing policies, task-fit evaluation, and organization-level defaults rather than one-size-fits-all assistant configuration.
findings.routing_note: Route model and product availability upstream; local wiki may capture model-routing governance and evaluation practice.

findings.summary: ITPro covered Gartner warnings that AI development efforts can incur higher costs when teams do not control tooling, context, review, and operational overhead.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Context architecture should include cost observability, context budgets, and workflow-level ROI review, especially when agents expand retrieval, planning, and verification work.
findings.routing_note: Route company background upstream; local wiki may capture cost-control and context-budget operating practices.

findings.summary: ExplainX published an MCP security guide discussing authentication, authorization, data exposure, tool governance, and operational controls.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: MCP usage in coding workflows should be treated as governed tool access: least privilege, tool allowlists, audit trails, data boundaries, and explicit approval gates should be part of local practice.
findings.routing_note: Route broad MCP protocol coverage upstream; local wiki may capture governed MCP practice for coding agents.

findings.summary: AI Eval Digest discussed agent evaluation environments, agreement among independent agents, and reliability patterns for evaluating AI systems.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Coding-agent evaluation should track trajectory behavior and cross-run agreement, not just final answer correctness, when calibrating review, repair, and planning loops.
findings.routing_note: Local wiki can capture the evaluation-design implication; broad research paper background may be routed upstream if durable entity pages are needed.

findings.summary: A practice essay described agent harnesses as the environment around an LLM, including information access, tools, context design, task constraints, and iterative feedback.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This reinforces local application-pattern coverage for harness architecture: context feeds, tool boundaries, feedback loops, and user-visible progress should be treated as first-class design surfaces.
findings.routing_note: Route Claude product/model background upstream; local wiki may capture harness architecture practice.
